adjacent angles: Two angles that share a common vertex and a common side but do not overlap.
angle addition postulate: If a ray lies inside an angle, the two smaller angles it forms add up to the whole angle.
angle bisector: A ray from an angle's vertex that splits the angle into two congruent halves.
betweenness: A point B is between A and C when the three points are collinear and AB + BC = AC.
collinear points: Three or more points that all lie on the same straight line.
complementary angles: Two angles whose measures add up to exactly 90 degrees.
conditional statement: A logical statement of the form 'if p, then q,' with hypothesis p and conclusion q.
congruent segments: Two line segments that have equal length, written with the congruence symbol.
converse, inverse, contrapositive: Variations of 'p → q': converse 'q → p,' inverse 'not p → not q,' contrapositive 'not q → not p.'
distance formula: The distance between two points: d = √((x₂−x₁)² + (y₂−y₁)²), from the Pythagorean theorem.
law of detachment / modus ponens: If 'p → q' is true and p is true, then q must be true.
law of syllogism: If 'p → q' and 'q → r' are both true, then 'p → r' is also true.
line segment: The straight path between two endpoints, having a finite, measurable length.
linear pair: Two adjacent angles whose non-common sides form a straight line, so they sum to 180 degrees.
midpoint formula: The midpoint of a segment: M = ((x₁+x₂)/2, (y₁+y₂)/2), the average of the endpoints' coordinates.
properties of congruence: Reflexive, symmetric, and transitive properties stating how congruence relations behave for segments and angles.
properties of equality: Rules (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, substitution, distributive) for operating on both sides of an equation.
reflexive property: Any segment or angle is congruent to itself.
segment bisector: A point, line, ray, or plane that divides a segment into two congruent parts at its midpoint.
supplementary angles: Two angles whose measures add up to exactly 180 degrees.
two-column proof: A proof with statements listed in the left column and their justifying reasons in the right column.
undefined terms: The basic, formally undefined concepts of geometry: point, line, and plane.
vertical angles: The pair of opposite angles formed when two lines cross; they are always congruent.
vertical angles theorem: When two lines intersect, the vertical (opposite) angles formed are congruent.
aa similarity postulate: If two angles of one triangle are congruent to two angles of another, the triangles are similar.
aas congruence theorem: Two triangles are congruent if two angles and a non-included side of one match those of the other.
alternate interior angles: A pair of angles between two lines on opposite sides of a transversal; congruent when the lines are parallel.
asa congruence postulate: Two triangles are congruent if two angles and the included side of one match those of the other.
co-interior / same-side interior angles: Angles between two lines on the same side of a transversal; supplementary when the lines are parallel.
converse of alternate interior angles th: If alternate interior angles formed by a transversal are congruent, the two lines are parallel.
converse of co-interior angles theorem: If same-side interior angles sum to 180 degrees, the two lines are parallel.
converse of corresponding angles postula: If corresponding angles formed by a transversal are congruent, the two lines are parallel.
correspondence in congruent triangles: The matching of vertices, sides, and angles between two congruent triangles, fixed by the naming order.
corresponding angles: Angles in the same relative position where a transversal crosses two lines; congruent when the lines are parallel.
corresponding parts of congruent triangl: Once two triangles are proven congruent, their matching sides and angles are congruent (CPCTC).
hl congruence theorem: Two right triangles are congruent if their hypotenuses and one pair of legs are congruent.
indirect measurement: Finding an unreachable length or height using proportions from similar triangles.
perimeter and area ratios: For similar figures with scale factor k, perimeters are in ratio k:1 and areas in ratio k²:1.
reflexive property of congruence: Any segment or angle is congruent to itself, often used for a shared side or angle in proofs.
sas congruence postulate: Two triangles are congruent if two sides and the included angle of one match those of the other.
sas similarity theorem: Triangles are similar if two pairs of sides are proportional and the included angles are congruent.
scale factor & proportion: The common ratio of corresponding sides in similar figures, used to set up and solve proportions.
sss congruence postulate: Two triangles are congruent if all three pairs of corresponding sides are congruent.
sss similarity theorem: Two triangles are similar if all three pairs of corresponding sides are proportional.
transversal: A line that crosses two or more other lines at distinct points.
triangle proportionality theorem: A line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides proportionally.
angle formed inside a circle — 두 현의 교점: An angle formed by two chords crossing inside a circle equals half the sum of the two intercepted arcs.
angle formed outside a circle — 두 할선/접선-: An angle with its vertex outside a circle equals half the difference of the intercepted arcs.
arc measure: The degree measure of an arc, equal to the central angle that subtends it.
central angle: An angle whose vertex is at the circle's center; its measure equals its intercepted arc.
composite figure: A shape made of two or more basic figures, whose area is found by adding or subtracting pieces.
convex polygon: A polygon in which every interior angle is less than 180 degrees.
exterior angle sum: The exterior angles of any convex polygon always add up to 360 degrees.
height / altitude: The perpendicular distance from a base to the opposite vertex or side, used in area formulas.
inscribed angle: An angle with its vertex on the circle and sides that are chords; equal to half its intercepted arc.
inscribed quadrilateral: A quadrilateral with all four vertices on a circle; its opposite angles are supplementary.
interior angle sum formula: The interior angles of an n-sided polygon sum to (n − 2) × 180 degrees.
intersecting chords segment product: When two chords cross, the products of their two segment lengths are equal.
isosceles trapezoid: A trapezoid with one pair of parallel sides and congruent legs, giving congruent base angles and equal diagonals.
parallelogram: A quadrilateral with both pairs of opposite sides parallel, so opposite sides and angles are congruent.
rectangle: A parallelogram with four right angles and congruent diagonals.
regular polygon: A polygon that is both equilateral (equal sides) and equiangular (equal angles).
rhombus: A parallelogram with four equal sides, whose diagonals are perpendicular and bisect the angles.
secant-tangent / secant-secant power of: From an external point, products of secant or tangent segment lengths to a circle are equal.
sector: The pie-shaped region of a circle bounded by two radii and the arc between them.
shoelace formula: A formula computing a polygon's area from its vertex coordinates: A = ½|Σ(xᵢyᵢ₊₁ − xᵢ₊₁yᵢ)|.
slope: The steepness of a line: m = (y₂−y₁)/(x₂−x₁), equal for parallels and negative reciprocals for perpendiculars.
30-60-90 triangle: A right triangle with 30° and 60° acute angles and side ratio 1 : √3 : 2.
45-45-90 triangle: A right triangle with two 45° angles and side ratio 1 : 1 : √2.
angle of depression: The downward angle from the horizontal to a line of sight aimed below the observer.
angle of elevation: The upward angle from the horizontal to a line of sight aimed above the observer.
converse of the pythagorean theorem: Comparing c² with a² + b² classifies a triangle as right, acute, or obtuse.
cosine, cos θ: The ratio of the adjacent side to the hypotenuse in a right triangle (CAH).
hypotenuse & legs: In a right triangle, the hypotenuse is the longest side opposite the right angle; the legs form it.
inverse trigonometric ratios: Functions (sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹, tan⁻¹) that find an angle from a given trigonometric ratio.
perpendicular auxiliary line: An added vertical line that creates a right triangle for solving elevation or depression problems.
prism & cylinder: Solids with two congruent parallel bases joined by sides; volume equals base area times height.
pyramid & cone: Solids with one base and an apex; volume equals one-third of base area times height.
pythagorean theorem: In a right triangle, a² + b² = c², where c is the hypotenuse.
pythagorean triple: A set of three positive integers a, b, c satisfying a² + b² = c², such as 3-4-5.
rationalizing the denominator: Rewriting a fraction so no radical remains in the denominator by multiplying by a suitable root.
reflection: A transformation that flips a figure across a line, keeping each point equidistant from that line.
rigid motion / isometry: A transformation (translation, reflection, rotation) that preserves size and shape, giving congruent images.
rotation: A transformation that turns a figure about a fixed center point by a given angle.
sine, sin θ: The ratio of the opposite side to the hypotenuse in a right triangle (SOH).
slant height: The distance from a cone's or pyramid's apex to the edge of its base, used in surface area.
sphere: A perfectly round solid with surface area 4πr² and volume (4/3)πr³.
tangent, tan θ: The ratio of the opposite side to the adjacent side in a right triangle (TOA).
translation: A transformation that slides every point of a figure the same distance in the same direction.
